title: Where Pets.com operated, and who surrounded it
lede: Pets.com ran its business from two warehouses, one in the Bay Area and one in Indiana. Its rivals and the retail chains behind them were mostly a few hours’ drive away in California.

figure.title: Pets.com, its rivals and its backers, 1999–2000
figure.whatItShows: where Pets.com leased offices and warehouses, where its rivals were, and who stood behind it. Step through the timeline: sites appear when they were leased and gray out when they closed.
figure.caption: Pins are placed at city level and nudged apart so they don’t overlap; a thin line joins a moved pin to its true location. Dashed rings show 1,000 miles straight-line from each warehouse. They aren’t carrier shipping zones, which the filings don’t disclose. Leases are from the S-1 and 10-K exhibits[^1][^6]. Base map: U.S. Census Bureau via us-atlas[^39].

pins.title: San Francisco offices
pins.text: 435 Brannan St (the S-1 address, leased Apr 8, 1999), 945 Bryant St (Sep 1999) and a King St warehouse (Sep 1999).

pins.title: Union City distribution center
pins.text: 33201 Dowe Ave: 143,232 sq ft, subleased Jul 1, 1999, plus an 84,000 sq ft Hayward satellite (Nov 1999).

pins.title: Greenwood, Indiana: second warehouse
pins.text: Leased Dec 7, 1999 near Indianapolis. Once it “reached its full load of U.S. shipping” in mid-2000, gross margin improved from −20% to −3%.

pins.title: Petstore.com, Emeryville
pins.text: Discovery-backed rival, bought by Pets.com in Jul 2000 for stock plus $3M cash.

pins.title: PetSmart.com, Pasadena
pins.text: A PetSmart/Idealab joint venture that used PetSmart’s catalog fulfillment. It pulled its $115M IPO in Nov 2000, then bought the pets.com domain.

pins.title: Amazon.com, Seattle
pins.text: Largest shareholder: 40.7% before the IPO and 30.4% after. It later said the stake was worth “down to zero.”

pins.title: Disney / Catalyst Investments, Burbank
pins.text: A Disney affiliate with 3.7%. ABC airtime worth $11.02M was paid for in Pets.com stock.

pins.title: PetSmart, Phoenix
pins.text: Parent of PetSmart.com. It raised its stake from 48% to 81% after the IPO was withdrawn.

pins.title: Petco, San Diego
pins.text: Backed Petopia and shipped its orders from Petco distribution centers, then bought Petopia’s assets in Dec 2000.

pins.title: Merrill Lynch, New York
pins.text: Led the Feb 2000 IPO, then approached 50+ potential buyers in 2000. Fewer than 8 would even visit.

steps.label: Feb 1999
steps.title: Pets.com begins operating
steps.text: It buys the pets.com domain and a web store from WebMagic. The backers and rivals that will shape its life are already on the map.

steps.label: Apr 1999
steps.title: Offices in San Francisco
steps.text: 435 Brannan St becomes the address in the S-1; Bryant St offices and a King St warehouse follow in September.

steps.label: Jul 1999
steps.title: Union City distribution center
steps.text: 143,232 sq ft in the East Bay. Goods plus shipping cost more than sales in every quarter reported.

steps.label: Dec 1999
steps.title: A second warehouse in Indiana
steps.text: Greenwood, near Indianapolis. Once at full load in mid-2000, gross margin went from −20% to −3%.

text: Once at full load, gross margin

steps.label: Feb 2000
steps.title: IPO at $11
steps.text: Merrill Lynch leads the IPO, raising $82.5M gross. Disney’s Catalyst already holds stock issued for ABC airtime.

text: Merrill Lynch led the IPO, then pitched

steps.label: Jul 2000
steps.title: Pets.com buys Petstore.com
steps.text: The Emeryville rival is acquired for stock plus $3M cash, a consolidation that came late.

steps.label: Nov 2000
steps.title: Closed virtual doors
steps.text: The wind-down is announced Nov 7; about 255 of 320 employees are laid off. PetSmart.com later buys the pets.com domain.

steps.label: Dec 2000
steps.title: Petco buys Petopia’s assets
steps.text: The San Diego retail chain picks up the rival it had backed. The independents are gone.

steps.label: Jan 2001
steps.title: Dissolved and delisted
steps.text: Stockholders approve the dissolution; the remaining staff resigned on Jan 16. Shareholders eventually got $0.172 a share back.

blocks.body: In 2000 the company said it had moved headquarters to a “new, larger facility”.[^4] We couldn’t confirm the address, so only leased addresses are shown. After dissolution, the company’s address was Diablo Management Group in Danville, CA.[^6]
